title: Concept Modulation Models: A Unified Framework for Identifiability and Extrapolation
claim: A unified model class can be analyzed geometrically: identifiability follows when valid transitions from each side intersect within a tolerated set.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid; graphical model, nested-set diagrams, Venn intersection
description: A 2x2 grid of four panels. Panel (a) is a small graphical model: a square node A, then shaded circles Λ and C, then a white circle X, joined by left-to-right arrows labeled Q, B and K. Panel (b) shows a red rounded rectangle for the model class K^mk(A→C) that contains a darker ellipse for the valid set. Inside, a point Q̄ has a solid arrow to a point inside the ellipse (labeled τ_v) and a dashed arrow to a point outside it (labeled τ_b). Panel (c) is the same layout in blue, for mixing maps K, K′ and K″. Panel (d) is a Venn diagram. A red ellipse and a blue ellipse overlap, and a tall black ellipse labeled 𝔊 crosses both. The color coding, red for concept and blue for mixing, ties the panels together. The eye goes first to the colored blobs.
caption: Overview of CMMs and transition constraints. (a) The observed attribute \(A\) influences a modulation variable \(\modrv\), which modulates the latent concept \(C\), which generates the observation \(X\). (b,c) Valid concept and mixing transitions are concept-space transformations that can be absorbed into the corresponding model class. Arrows in (b) denote equivalence after restriction to \(\cAo\), while arrows in (c) read \(\bK \refmeq \bK'\Push_{\tau_v} \refmeq \bK"\Push_{\tau_b}\). (d) The transition-intersection criterion selects transitions valid on both sides; if their intersection is contained in \(\frakG\), the CMM is identifiable up to \(\sim_\frakG\) ([ref]).
abstract: Reliable generalization in conditional latent variable models requires understanding both identifiability and extrapolation: how observed variation across attributes determines latent structure, and how that structure determines distributions at unseen attributes. However, existing identifiability and extrapolation guarantees are largely model-specific, with separate analyses in nonlinear ICA, causal representation learning, perturbation modeling, and related conditional latent variable models. We introduce concept modulation models (CMMs), an attribute-indexed class of conditional generative models with structure $A\to Î\to C\to X$, where attributes select modulators, modulators induce latent concept laws, and concepts generate observed features. CMMs lift transition-based identifiability to conditional settings by showing that feature agreement on observed attributes induces a latent concept transition constrained by the CMM class. We express these constraints through attribute potentials, log-density ratios between attribute-conditioned concept laws, separating the generic lifting step from model-specific rigidity arguments. The same potentials control extrapolation: agreement at unseen attributes holds exactly when the transported attribute-potential identities extend to those attributes. This yields algebraic extrapolation criteria, identifies the common potential-based proof objects behind several existing identifiability and extrapolation results, and, when combined with the model-specific rigidity arguments in those works, recovers their stated conclusions.
